name: Colosseum
modelNote: Rings, heights and the standing arc of the outer wall from OpenStreetMap’s 3D outline; dimensions and dates from the sources. Seating, underground galleries and decoration are schematic.

evidence.identity: Colosseo (Flavian Amphitheatre), Piazza del Colosseo, Rome, Italy (OSM relation 1834818)
features: An ellipse of 189 × 156 m, outer wall 48 m high (Wikipedia).
Three storeys of arcades framed by engaged columns, and a tall attic with pilasters and windows (Wikipedia).
240 mast corbels round the top of the attic for the velarium (Wikipedia).
The outer wall stands only on the north side; on the south side the inner ring is exposed (OpenStreetMap 3D outline: outer part 48.5 m, inner ring 36 m, cavea 24 and 12 m).
Two 19th-century props at the ends of the standing outer wall (1807 and 1827): a sloping brick wedge at one end, brick arches rebuilt in steps at the other (Wikipedia; shapes read from photos).
evidence.geometry: Ellipse centre, axis (18.6° from east towards south) and ring sizes fitted to the OpenStreetMap building parts: outer wall 94.5 × 78 m semi-axes, inner ring 81.1 × 64.4 m, cavea steps at 78.2 × 57.8 m (24 m) and 65.6 × 49.3 m (12 m). The standing outer wall runs from about 184° to 356° (north side). Arena 87 × 55 m (Wikipedia).
uncertainties: Storey heights of the outer wall (10.5, 11.8, 11.6 m and a 14.6 m attic) shared from the 48.5 m total.
80 bays per ring; arches, columns and attic simplified.
Seating raked in one slope; the timber upper gallery and its fire of 217 are not shown.
Underground galleries drawn as parallel walls, not their real plan.
Which end dates from 1807 and which from 1827 is not stated in the sources used; the wedge (east) and the stepped arches (west) follow photos.

phases.title: Vespasian’s amphitheatre
phases.text: Vespasian starts the amphitheatre around 70–72. By his death in 79, three storeys of arcades ring the arena and the seating rises inside.

moments.title: Stone without mortar
moments.text: Over 100,000 m³ of travertine are set without mortar, held together by 300 tonnes of iron clamps.

phases.title: Titus opens it
phases.text: His son Titus finishes the top level in 80 and opens the amphitheatre with games in which, according to Dio Cassius, over 9,000 wild animals are killed.

moments.title: An awning for 50,000
moments.text: 240 mast corbels round the top of the attic hold the velarium, a retractable awning worked by sailors from Misenum that shades two thirds of the arena.

phases.title: Under the arena
phases.text: Domitian adds the hypogeum, a network of tunnels below the arena floor for animals and slaves, and a gallery at the top for more seats.

moments.title: A machine under the sand
moments.text: From the hypogeum, animals and scenery could be brought up into the arena without being seen.

phases.title: Struck by lightning
phases.text: A fire started by lightning, says Dio Cassius, destroys the wooden upper levels. Repairs are not finished until about 240.

moments.title: Twenty years of repairs
moments.text: The 217 fire closes the upper levels for two decades: the repairs are only complete around 240.

phases.title: The south side falls
phases.text: An earthquake brings down the outer wall on the south side, which stood on less stable alluvial ground. The inner ring is left exposed.

moments.title: Built on two grounds
moments.text: The south side stood on alluvial ground, less stable than the north: that is the side that collapsed in 1349.

phases.title: A quarry for Rome
phases.text: The fallen stone is carted off for palaces, churches and hospitals, and marble is burned for quicklime. The seats disappear; the vaults that carried them remain.

moments.title: Why the walls are pitted
moments.text: The iron clamps holding the stones were pried and hacked out, leaving the pockmarks that still scar the building.

phases.title: Brick wedges
phases.text: In 1807 and 1827 the cut ends of the standing outer wall are propped up: on one side a sloping brick spur, on the other brick arches rebuilt in steps, in the shape of the originals.

moments.title: Holding the broken ends
moments.text: Where the outer ring stops, one end leans on a brick wedge; at the other, new brick arches step down like a staircase of the old ones.

phases.title: Cleaned
phases.text: A restoration sponsored by Diego Della Valle cleans the façade from 2013; the work is finished on 1 July 2016.

moments.title: €25 million
moments.text: Diego Della Valle agrees to fund a €25 million restoration; the cleaning of the façade ends on 1 July 2016.
